clue.text: Vile prison meal, cold

indicators.note: something vile is twisted and corrupt, so the letters of the two words are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A grumble about disgusting jail food served without heating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cold' looks like part of the food complaint, but it is the definition, in its sense of a manner lacking warmth.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym in the emotional sense: an aloof, detached manner lacking warmth or personal feeling.

clue.text: Couple I came upon going north

indicators.note: in a down clue, going north means reading upward, so the word for came upon is turned backwards

parts.note: to come upon someone is to meet them, past tense met

explanation.surface: Someone recalls meeting a pair while travelling north.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: a romantic pair are described as being an item, so the word stands for a couple.

clue.text: Speak with another about southern herb

indicators.note: the talk word goes about, that is around, the single letter for southern

parts.note: to parley is to hold talks with someone, especially an opponent

explanation.surface: Chatting with someone about a herb from the south.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a common green culinary plant used for garnish and flavouring, a classic kitchen herb.

clue.text: Nuts and drinks for all in group before dance

indicators.note: in a down clue the drinks piece comes before, above, the dance

parts.note: buying a round means getting drinks for everyone in the party
the Twist is the 1960s dance popularised by Chubby Checker

explanation.surface: A night out: nuts and a round of drinks for the gang, then dancing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nuts' looks like bar snacks but is the definition, meaning crazy; ROUND THE TWIST is British slang for mad.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang synonym: both describe someone who has gone mad or lost their reason.

clue.text: Submissive, one during depression, following order

indicators.note: the dent-with-one piece comes after the honour, following it

parts.note: OBE is the Order of the British Empire

indicators.note: the numeral one sits during, that is within, the hollow

parts.note: a dent is a small hollow or depression in a surface
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A meek person, following orders while depressed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'order' looks like a command to obey but is the British honour OBE; 'following' puts that before DIENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a submissive person is compliant and willing to do as they are told.

clue.text: Tolerate fat? Not initially

indicators.note: the word for fat loses its opening letter, being not there initially

parts.note: tallow is hard animal fat used for candles and soap

explanation.surface: A question about whether to put up with fatness.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to tolerate something is to permit it or let it happen.

clue.text: Heather wanting a boy

indicators.note: wanting means lacking, so the plant name goes without the letter a

parts.note: erica is the botanical genus name for heather

explanation.surface: A woman named Heather longs for a son.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heather' looks like a woman's name but is the plant, ERICA.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a common male first name, standing for any boy in crossword convention.

clue.text: Practical type is later converted

indicators.note: converted means changed into another form, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A pragmatic person becomes a convert later on.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a pragmatist who deals with things as they are rather than as one might wish.

clue.text: Means of buying goods vehicle loaded outside

indicators.note: the word for loaded sits outside, around, the vehicle

parts.note: a gun or battery that is loaded is charged
a car is a vehicle

explanation.surface: A goods vehicle being loaded up with cargo outside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'goods vehicle' reads as a lorry, but 'goods' ends the definition and 'vehicle' is CAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a plastic card used to pay for purchases on account, a way of buying things.

clue.text: On the way out, collared by class first off

indicators.note: a collar goes round the neck, so the word out is held within the trimmed class word
the class word loses its first letter

parts.note: a genre is a class or category of art or writing

explanation.surface: Someone on their way out is arrested by a class at the start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' reads as part of the definition phrase 'on the way out', but the definition stops at 'way'.
explanation.definitionFit: Borrowed French phrase used in English for something in transit, during the journey.

clue.text: Renowned mathematician not keeping quiet inside the French opera house

indicators.note: the trimmed scientist's name goes inside the French article

parts.note: la is a French word for the

indicators.note: the mathematician's name does not keep the letter for quiet

parts.note: Blaise Pascal was a famous French mathematician
p is the musical abbreviation for piano, quiet

explanation.surface: A famous mathematician noisily inside a French opera house.
explanation.definitionFit: Proper name: Milan's celebrated theatre is one of the world's best-known venues for opera.

clue.text: Goon in lace factory I find fault with on the way up

parts.note: to lace a drink with alcohol is to spike it
a mill is a factory

indicators.note: in a down clue, on the way up means read upward, so the fault-finding word is turned backwards

parts.note: to nag is to keep finding fault with someone

explanation.surface: A thug in a lace factory, with someone criticising him upstairs.
explanation.walkthrough: The Goons were a 1950s British radio comedy troupe; Spike Milligan was their chief writer. 'Goon' looks like a thug.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the comedian was a member of the Goon Show cast, so he is one Goon.

clue.text: Breaking a law? Indignity for royal attendant

indicators.note: breaking breaks the words apart so their letters can be reassembled

explanation.surface: Someone at court breaks the law, an embarrassment for a royal servant.
explanation.definitionFit: Title: a woman of the court who attends a queen or princess, a royal companion.

clue.text: So pretence is ridiculous, if this?

definitions.text: So pretence is ridiculous, if this?

indicators.note: ridiculous means absurd and nonsensical, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Pretending is absurd if everybody already knows the truth.
explanation.walkthrough: Read whole, the clue is the definition too: pretending to keep something quiet is silly when everyone knows it.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: a supposed confidence that is in fact widely known to everyone.

clue.text: Deliriously happy on end of line in call-box?

indicators.note: delirious means wildly disordered, so the letters of the word happy are scrambled
the end of the word line is its final letter

explanation.surface: Someone thrilled at the end of a phone line.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags 'call-box' as a definition by example of a public telephone.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a British call-box is a public telephone operated by coins or cards.

clue.text: Reportedly dispose of second Scottish club

indicators.note: reportedly means as heard, so the phrase is said aloud

parts.note: to dispose of goods is to sell them; a tick is a second, a brief moment

explanation.surface: News that a Scottish club is getting rid of a second-string player.
explanation.walkthrough: SELL plus TICK, said aloud, give the club's name, pronounced with a soft C. Celtic is a Glasgow football club.
explanation.definitionFit: Proper name: the Glasgow football side is one of Scotland's best-known clubs.

clue.text: Supposing I put in condition daughter tweaked

indicators.note: the supposing word and I are put inside the condition word

parts.note: a mode is a state or condition, as in survival mode
if means supposing that

explanation.surface: A parent wonders about putting a daughter into some condition.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: both describe something changed slightly or adjusted.

clue.text: Refinement in French resort city? Not western half

parts.note: Nice is a resort on the French Riviera

indicators.note: an across word read left to right has its western half first, so the first two letters go

explanation.surface: Sophistication in a Riviera town, minus its western quarter.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a fine detail or subtle point of refinement, as in the niceties of etiquette.

clue.text: Burst into tears upon tide rising, and give a false alarm

indicators.note: in a down clue the tears word sits upon, above, the tide word

parts.note: to cry is to burst into tears

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means read upward, so the tide word is turned backwards

parts.note: the flow is the incoming tide

explanation.surface: Someone weeps at the rising tide and raises a needless alarm.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom from Aesop's boy who shouted about a wolf: to raise an alarm that is not genuine.

clue.text: Changing of editor becomes highly desirable

indicators.note: changing the letters means putting them in a different order

explanation.surface: A newspaper's change of editor becomes something everyone wants.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: something so desirable that one would give anything to have it.

clue.text: Fleet clear to find shipping forecast area

parts.note: fleet-footed means fast
to net a sum is to clear it as profit

explanation.surface: A fleet of ships is told the way is clear for a sea area.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fleet' reads as a group of ships but means quick. The Shipping Forecast is the BBC radio sea weather bulletin; Fastnet is one of its areas, off south-west Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: Proper name: one of the sea regions named in the BBC's maritime weather bulletin.

clue.text: See Welsh girl Gracie, perhaps, in a state of perfect happiness

parts.note: a see is a bishop's seat; Ely is a cathedral city and diocese
Sian is a Welsh girl's name
Gracie Fields was a popular English singer and actress of the 1930s

explanation.surface: Look at Welsh girl Gracie, apparently blissfully happy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See' looks like a command to look but is a bishop's diocese, here ELY. Gracie Fields was a much-loved British music-hall singer.
explanation.definitionFit: Myth: the Greek paradise of the blessed, used figuratively for a place or state of bliss.

clue.text: Opera embraced by Cameron or May

indicators.note: the opera's title is held within the run of letters, embraced by these words

explanation.surface: An opera hugged by two former British prime ministers.
explanation.walkthrough: David Cameron and Theresa May were UK prime ministers; the definition is Bellini's opera.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: Bellini's tragic bel canto work about a druid priestess is a well-known opera.

clue.text: Poor show

definitions.meaning: poor in the sense of shabby or inferior
to show or signify, as in what does this indicate

explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: shabby and inferior, and to signify or indicate something.

clue.text: Domestic cock and duck in list

indicators.note: the duck letter goes in the list word

parts.note: a roster is a list of names on duty
a duck is a score of nought in cricket, hence the letter O

explanation.surface: A farmyard cockerel and a duck are on the list.
explanation.walkthrough: 'duck' looks like another farm bird but is cricket's zero, O.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: the male of the domestic chicken, chiefly in American usage.

clue.text: Artless young woman's true home at the beginning

indicators.note: the home letters are taken out of the word for true and put at its beginning

parts.note: genuine means true or real
in means at home

explanation.surface: A naive young woman's truthful home life in its early days.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a naive, innocent girl, especially as a stock theatrical role.

clue.text: Difficult losing second pet

indicators.note: the word for difficult loses the letter for second

parts.note: a stiff test is a difficult one

explanation.surface: A tough moment as a second pet is lost.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pet' looks like an animal but is the noun for a fit of sulking, as in 'in a pet'.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a pet is a sulk or fit of pique; a minor quarrel or huff.

clue.text: Hot air not circulating in London station

parts.note: padding is wordy filler, empty talk

indicators.note: circulating means going round, so the word not is turned backwards

explanation.surface: Stale air not moving in a London railway station.
explanation.definitionFit: Proper name: a major London railway terminus, also giving its name to the famous bear.
